facts.text: Challenger Descent Stage was deployed at Taurus-Littrow during Apollo 17 in 1972.
Lower half of Lunar Module Challenger. The last crewed spacecraft to land on the Moon. Cernan and Schmitt spent a record 75 hours on the surface with three EVAs totalling 22 hours.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Supported the longest crewed stay on the Moon (74.6 hours), demonstrating that humans could conduct sustained scientific fieldwork on another world.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Taurus-Littrow.
Remains in Taurus-Littrow valley; the last crewed spacecraft on the lunar surface. Its plaque reads: 'Here Man completed his first explorations of the Moon.'
